prompt:
A modern country song, 90 seconds, with a real lead vocal. Male vocal with a warm southern drawl, plainspoken and lived-in, singing a story. THE BAND MUST BE LOUD, FULL AND PRESENT FROM THE FIRST BAR — this is a proper record with a singer on it, not a vocal with something faint underneath. Mixed loud and modern, full low end. Acoustic guitar strumming hard, crying pedal steel answering every line, tight snare with brushes then sticks, walking upright bass, a little honky-tonk piano, fiddle coming in on the chorus. Around 88 bpm, major key, proud and a bit weary. Sung, not rapped. Lyrics:

[Verse 1]
The sign out front still says we're open till two
And I'm the last one here with a job left to do
Momma said go find something steady and sure
So I found me a fryer and a hard locked door

[Chorus]
And it ain't much but it's mine
Every bolt of it, every line
You can walk on up and read it on the wall
That's the honest part, that's all
That's the honest part, that's all

[Verse 2]
I seen the fast ones come and I seen em go
Ridin high on a promise they was never gonna owe
I ain't got a promise, I ain't got a pitch
Just a light on late and an honest ditch

[Chorus]
And it ain't much but it's mine
Every bolt of it, every line
You can walk on up and read it on the wall
That's the honest part, that's all
